rows.text: Every Sliver you cast cascades — and a cascade cast is still a CAST, so if the free spell is also a Sliver, it cascades too. One five-drop Sliver chains down through the whole curve, and each link is another body, another anthem, and another enters-the-battlefield trigger shared by the entire board. The deck is not really a tribal aggro deck. It is a combo deck whose combo is "cast a Sliver".

rows.name: The First Sliver
rows.text: five colours, a 7/7, and every Sliver spell you cast has cascade. Once he is out, the correct play is almost always "cast the most expensive Sliver in hand" — the chain does the rest.

rows.name: Morophon, the Boundless
rows.text: name Sliver and every Sliver spell costs {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} less. Most of the deck becomes free, and each free cast still cascades.

rows.name: Maelstrom Nexus
rows.text: the first spell you cast each turn cascades, Sliver or not.

rows.name: Quandrix, the Proof
rows.text: your instants and sorceries from hand cascade too.

rows.name: Maelstrom Wanderer
rows.text: two more cascades, and permanent haste for the whole board — which matters because the chain deploys creatures mid-turn.

rows.name: Apex Devastator
rows.text: four cascades on one card.

rows.name: Call Forth the Tempest
rows.text: two cascades plus a sweeper sized by everything the chain has already cast.

rows.name: Averna, the Chaos Bloom
rows.text: every cascade also puts a land onto the battlefield, so a long chain ramps you at the same time.

guide.title: Getting paid for the free casts

rows.name: Nalfeshnee
rows.text: every spell cast from exile is COPIED. A cascade chain with Nalfeshnee out doubles every Sliver in it.

rows.name: Quintorius Kand
rows.text: two damage to each opponent and two life to you for EVERY spell cast from exile. A six-link chain is twelve damage to the table before combat.

rows.name: Lavabelly Sliver
rows.text: every Sliver that enters pings a player for one and gains you one. During a chain, that is one trigger per link, on top of everything else.

rows.name: Harmonic Sliver
rows.text: every Sliver that enters destroys an artifact or enchantment. A cascade chain becomes a one-sided Vandalblast on the table's whole board.

rows.name: Guardian Project
rows.text: a card for every differently named nontoken creature — and every Sliver in the deck has a different name.

rows.name: Kindred Discovery
rows.text: name Sliver. A card for every Sliver that enters AND every one that attacks.

guide.title: The mana that makes it possible

rows.name: Gemhide Sliver
rows.text: all Slivers tap for any colour. Two Slivers later this is a five-colour mana engine.

rows.name: Manaweft Sliver
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Basal Sliver
rows.text: every Sliver can sacrifice for {B}{B}, which is how you convert a huge board into a huge spell.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: turn-one fixing.

rows.name: Bloom Tender
rows.text: scales with your colours.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: uncounterable mana for legendary spells — The First Sliver himself.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: an untapped dual.

rows.name: Farseek
rows.text: a shockland.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: usually taps for exactly what you are missing.

rows.name: Lotus Bloom
rows.text: suspend it on turn one and it is three mana of any colour on turn four.
Suspended cards are cast for free from EXILE when their last counter is removed, which triggers Nalfeshnee and Quintorius Kand just like a cascade does.

rows.name: Ancestral Vision
rows.text: three cards for one mana, four turns later.

rows.name: Inevitable Betrayal
rows.text: the best creature out of an opponent's library, onto your battlefield.

rows.name: Profane Tutor
rows.text: any card in the deck for two mana on a delay.

rows.name: Lotus Bloom
rows.text: acceleration with no card cost.

rows.name: Predatory Sliver
rows.text: +1/+1 to the whole team.

rows.name: Cloudshredder Sliver
rows.text: flying AND haste for every Sliver. It is what turns a cascade chain into a lethal attack the same turn.

rows.name: Galerider Sliver
rows.text: the one-mana flying anthem.

rows.name: Bonescythe Sliver
rows.text: double strike for the whole board.

rows.name: Leeching Sliver
rows.text: a life off the defending player for every Sliver that attacks.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: with your commander out, take both halves. On a wide Sliver board it simply ends the game.

rows.name: Crystalline Sliver
rows.text: all Slivers have shroud. Nothing they play can target your board — but note it stops your own targeting too.

rows.name: Diffusion Sliver
rows.text: the gentler version, taxing their removal two.

rows.name: Hibernation Sliver
rows.text: every Sliver can bounce itself for two life, saving it from removal or resetting an enters trigger.

rows.name: Quick Sliver
rows.text: Slivers gain flash, so you can build the board at the end of their turn.

rows.name: Necrotic Sliver
rows.text: every Sliver can sacrifice to destroy any permanent. On a wide board that is unlimited removal.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: hexproof and indestructible through a wrath.

rows.name: Assassin's Trophy
rows.text: two mana for any permanent.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: overloaded, the clear for a lethal attack.

rows.name: Raise the Palisade
rows.text: name Sliver and every other creature at the table goes back to hand. A one-sided bounce wrath.

rows.name: Patriarch's Bidding
rows.text: name Sliver. You rebuild your entire graveyard; most tables get far less back.

rows.name: Homing Sliver
rows.text: gives every Sliver in hand slivercycling, so dead cards become the exact Sliver you need.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the best card in the deck on turns one through four.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep fixing and a cheap Sliver. Gemhide Sliver or Manaweft Sliver on turn two solves the five-colour problem by itself, because every Sliver you play afterwards is also a mana source.
The First Sliver costs five specific colours. Prioritise Morophon, the mana Slivers and Bloom Tender over another anthem — the deck does nothing until he resolves, and everything once he does.
Cast the most expensive Sliver first. Cascade finds a cheaper card, so leading with a five-drop chains through four-, three-, two- and one-drops; leading with a one-drop finds nothing.

rows.name: Cloudshredder Sliver
rows.text: keep it in mind before you start the chain. Flying and haste means the board you just built attacks this turn, which is usually the difference between a big turn and a lethal one.
